newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts high court overturns term limits law.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts high court overturns term limits law.

text.p: Massachusetts' highest court Friday struck down the state's term limit law that bars politicians from seeking re-election after two terms in a particular office.
The Massachusetts State Supreme Court ruled that the law, which was narrowly passed by voters in a 1994 referendum, was unconstitutional.
"I am furious," said Dorothea Vitrac, the head of Limits II, a citizens group that helped draft the law angered by the raises and perks legislators had given themselves.

"The court receives its pay and its budget from the Legislature. They're not about to bite the hand that feeds them and limit the terms," she said. "The Massachusetts State Supreme Court, when it comes to the Legislature, are holding hands. They're in bed together."
Limits II will review the ruling before considering its next move, she said.

Earlier this month, Massachusetts House Speaker Thomas Finneran, a Democrat, rewarded key legislators - the chairmen and vice chairmen and ranking Republicans of the Rules and Long Term Debt committees and four division chairs - with bonus pay retroactive to January 1996.
Finneran said the raise was to "reward good work."
But other legislators, especially the Republican minority, have sought to overturn the speaker's largesse. A rollcall vote on the raises is set for next week.
